## Highlights since 0.4.0

- **One collaboration timeline.** Versions, activity and Overleaf history share one timeline. Read changes by sentence and resolve a conflict by choosing a side.
- **Overleaf conversations beside the work.** Comments, suggestions and chat read as conversations, with one colour per person and presence showing who is where. Margin review places comments and suggestions beside their lines while keeping at least 88 columns for the text.
- **A redesigned Git panel.** Changes, Pull requests and In the paper provide focused views, with a matching loading skeleton and a Code review inbox that follows the app language.
- **Highlighters with meanings.** Six highlighters apply with one click; Annotations groups the marks by meaning.
- **Faster startup, screens and scrolling.** Repeated launches skip a redundant bundle walk measured at about 599 ms. In the WebKit browser benchmark, the first editable document appeared in 375 ms instead of 608 ms, and the first PDF page in 612 ms instead of 1,060 ms. Add papers first opened in 93 ms instead of 338 ms. With 600 papers, the longest scroll frame fell from 148 to 33 ms, and the first search keystroke from 300–309 to 41–44 ms. These are measured before/after fixtures, not release-app timing guarantees; details and measurement conditions are in [the performance notes](https://github.com/leo1oel/lattice/blob/v0.5.0/docs/performance.md).
- **Calmer motion.** Margin review cards and rails ease in and out, and the new collaboration and Git surfaces use the app's motion tiers.

## Notable fixes

- Papers load with clear loading, syncing and error states; narrow rows keep their keys and actions inside the row, and downloads can be cancelled.
- Add papers and manual entry share one sheet; Check references has an inline tri-state Select all and distinct, named status marks.
- The bibliography list has a draggable divider and better narrow layouts. Outlines and the command palette use the app scrollbar and keep hover fills within their rows.
- The status bar folds items into More as space narrows; the Panels menu controls panel visibility, and editor and panel tab strips share one surface.
- Providers, MCP and Skills settings open on the right surface. Agent starters clear the composer, and the model picker and Pull requests view follow the app language.
- Inserting a Mermaid block leaves the caret in the paragraph after it. Tiptap is updated to 3.32.0, preserving the node-view caret fix.
- Settings regain focus when a covering shell closes, and history's Yesterday label handles clock changes correctly.
- Development checks now target changed code, preserve benchmark failure screenshots, build the CI benchmark page once, and track flaky tests with one automatic rerun on main.
